description: Breach notification clocks for Canadian privacy regimes, verified against primary sources. Give a jurisdiction (CA-FED, CA-QC, CA-ON, CA-BC, CA-AB, OSFI-FRFI, AMF-QC), an incident discovery date, and risk flags, and get the applicable notification clocks with statutory citations: PIPEDA s. 10.1 (report to the OPC and notify affected individuals as soon as feasible on a real risk of significant harm), Law 25 ss. 3.5 to 3.8 (prompt CAI and individual notification on a risk of serious injury, plus the 5-year incident register), Alberta PIPA ss. 34.1 and 37.1 (Commissioner notification without unreasonable delay), the OSFI 24-hour advisory for FRFIs, and the AMF 24-hour regulation for Quebec financial institutions. Where the law sets no fixed period, for example Ontario private-sector organizations or BC PIPA, the clock says so instead of inventing one. Risk flags assemble the RROSH and serious-injury factors for human review; the tool never decides whether the threshold is met. Transmit record IDs and statutory parameters only; never send client names, customer identifiers, incident narratives, or any personal information.

incident_discovery_date.description: Date the incident was discovered, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be a real calendar date and not in the future.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction scoping the clocks: federal PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25, Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta PIPA, OSFI-regulated financial institutions, or AMF-regulated Quebec institutions.

risk_flags.description: Risk flags shaping the threshold factors, for example financial_information or ransomware_or_malicious_actor. They guide the assessment; they never decide it.
